description:
Let AI agents, scripts and the people you hire use your API keys without ever seeing them.

Unseenkey keeps your API keys in an encrypted vault on your machine and hands out handles instead.
A handle looks like a key to the SDK that receives it, but it only works through the local broker,
which swaps it for the real key at the last moment, checks a policy (host, endpoints, rate, expiry,
approval), scrubs the key out of responses and writes every call to a tamper-evident audit log.
Includes an MCP server for Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor and Windsurf, Windows Hello unlock,
and signed auto-updates.
Security fixes for every earlier version: a handle could send the real key to another host through a
crafted wildcard host, a Supabase or Jira key could go to a stranger's project, `..` got past policies,
and a failed key test could show the key. After updating, run `usk daemon restart`. Existing Supabase
and Jira keys need their own host named once. Also: Google service account keys, two-part keys such as
Twilio, seven new providers, `usk passwd`, and one-command setup with `usk mcp install`.
Not yet externally audited; installer not code-signed.
